message.content:
The exact count of mitochondria can vary widely depending on the cell type, its metabolic demands, and its stage of differentiation or activity. In general:

| Cell type (or condition) | Typical mitochondrial count per cell |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Typical mammalian somatic cell** | ~500–2000 mitochondria |
| **Highly active muscle or nerve cells** | >10 000 mitochondria (especially in cardiac myocytes) |
| **Stem cells or proliferating cells** | ~200–800 mitochondria |
| **Cancer cells (often high metabolic rate)** | Can exceed 10 000 in some cases |

So while there isn’t a single “number” that applies universally, most normal human cells contain roughly **hundreds to a few thousand mitochondria**, with specialized cells like heart muscle cells having tens of thousands.
